metadata.title: Ghost Tools Enhanced Configuration
metadata.description: Ghost tools configuration upgraded with learnings from GEMS forensic system analysis

learnings_applied.name: Forensic vs Execution Separation
learnings_applied.description: Forensic systems are read-only, immutable-record domains. Execution systems are read-write and complex. Mixing both causes duplication, complexity, and coupling.
detection_rules: Flag components with dual roles (storage + instantiation, routing + validation)
Alert on mutable fields in audit-critical structures
Warn about intermediate state tracking (CREATED, RUNNING) in forensic context

learnings_applied.name: Copy-Paste Specialization Pattern
learnings_applied.description: Identical constructors/methods across specialized classes indicate over-specialization. Generic pattern (Registry/Router) often sufficient.
detection_rules: Detect 4+ functions with identical AST structure (copy-paste inheritance)
Flag specialized classes with only name/field differences
Recommend generic factory or registry pattern instead

learnings_applied.name: Orchestration-Driven Complexity
learnings_applied.description: Long functions (80+ lines) typically indicate orchestration logic. Forensic systems should avoid orchestration; instead use immutable records + queries.
detection_rules: Functions 80+ lines: likely orchestration (80-134 line range)
Complex state machine implementations: orchestration smell
Workflow coordination logic: execution-specific, not forensic

learnings_applied.name: Single Responsibility Verification
learnings_applied.description: Each component should have exactly one responsibility. Dual-role components (e.g., Registry doing storage + instantiation) signal missing abstraction.
detection_rules: Flag components with 'and' in responsibility description
Detect Registry with instantiation logic (should be storage only)
Detect Router with validation logic (should be routing only)

learnings_applied.name: Frozen Dataclass for Audit Trail
learnings_applied.description: Forensic audit trails require immutable, tamper-proof records. Use frozen dataclasses for Artifact, Provenance, Handoff.
detection_rules: Flag non-frozen dataclasses in audit-critical paths
Alert on mutable fields (dict, list) in immutable structures
Recommend @dataclass(frozen=True) for forensic records

learnings_applied.name: Final vs Intermediate States
learnings_applied.description: Forensic systems only see final states (COMPLETED, FAILED). Tracking intermediate states (CREATED, RUNNING) adds complexity without value.
detection_rules: Detect Enum with 4+ states including CREATED/RUNNING
Flag intermediate state tracking in forensic context
Recommend 2-state system (final outcomes only)

learnings_applied.name: Minimal Layer Stack
learnings_applied.description: Forensic systems need 3 layers: Data (immutable), Discovery (Registry/Router), Governance (validation). Execution layer is not forensic.
detection_rules: Alert on 4+ orchestration layers
Flag WorkflowCoordinator-like classes (execution orchestration)
Verify layer stack matches: Data → Discovery → Governance

learnings_applied.name: Query-Driven vs Imperative
learnings_applied.description: Forensic systems should be pull-based (queries) not push-based (orchestration). Pull model is simpler and more testable.
detection_rules: Flag push-based coordination patterns
Recommend pull-based query model for forensics
Alert on imperative WorkflowCoordinator-style patterns

learnings_applied.name: Minimal Systems are Highest Quality
learnings_applied.description: Code quality improves dramatically as complexity decreases. Stripping from 2500 to 173 lines reduced defects from 34 to 0.
detection_rules: Track defect count vs code size (inverse correlation)
Alert when system grows beyond essential components
Recommend aggressive removal of non-essential code

learnings_applied.name: Forensic System Axioms
learnings_applied.description: Forensic systems are fundamentally different from execution systems. Key axioms: read-only, immutable records, query-driven, tamper-proof.
detection_rules: Flag write operations on forensic records
Alert on mutable forensic data structures
Verify immutability of audit trail components

duplication_patterns.name: copy_paste_inheritance
duplication_patterns.description: Multiple classes with identical __init__ methods (only names differ)
duplication_patterns.example: architecture.py, requirements.py, researcher.py, reviewer.py all have same __init__
duplication_patterns.solution: Use generic base class or factory pattern instead
duplication_patterns.learned_from: GEMS specialist gem duplication (4 identical constructors)

duplication_patterns.name: repeated_validation_blocks
duplication_patterns.description: Same validation logic repeated in multiple branches
duplication_patterns.solution: Extract into single shared validation function

duplication_patterns.name: hand_built_object_patterns
duplication_patterns.description: Multiple code sections hand-building same object type

complexity_patterns.name: orchestration_function
complexity_patterns.description: Functions 80+ lines typically orchestrating multiple steps
complexity_patterns.solution: Extract orchestration into separate coordinator, split concerns

complexity_patterns.name: state_machine_implementation
complexity_patterns.example: Manually implementing state machine with 4+ states
complexity_patterns.solution: Use immutable records instead of state tracking

complexity_patterns.name: nested_branching
complexity_patterns.solution: Decompose into smaller functions, use pattern matching

dead_code_patterns.name: unused_initializer
dead_code_patterns.solution: Remove unused code or integrate into active path

dead_code_patterns.name: vestigial_specialization
dead_code_patterns.description: Specialized classes no longer used after refactoring
dead_code_patterns.example: Gem classes kept after routing logic changed
dead_code_patterns.solution: Remove after verifying nothing references them

dead_code_patterns.name: test_data_in_production
dead_code_patterns.description: Test/example data included in production code
dead_code_patterns.solution: Move to test files or remove

architectural_patterns.name: dual_responsibility_component
architectural_patterns.description: Component doing two distinct jobs (e.g., storage + instantiation)
architectural_patterns.example: Registry both storing and instantiating Gems
architectural_patterns.solution: Separate into two components with single responsibility each

architectural_patterns.name: forensic_execution_mixing
architectural_patterns.description: Audit/forensic code mixed with execution orchestration
architectural_patterns.example: Handoff with routing_signal and workflow_state fields

architectural_patterns.name: over_specialization
architectural_patterns.description: Specialized implementations where generic would suffice
architectural_patterns.example: 4 different gem classes with identical structure
architectural_patterns.solution: Use registry/factory pattern with generic implementations

immutability_patterns.name: mutable_audit_field
immutability_patterns.description: Mutable field in component that should be tamper-proof
immutability_patterns.example: Dict/list fields in Artifact, Provenance, Handoff
immutability_patterns.solution: Use frozen dataclass, immutable types (tuple, frozendict)

immutability_patterns.name: execution_metadata_in_record
immutability_patterns.description: Execution-specific fields in forensic audit records
immutability_patterns.solution: Keep audit records pure (remove execution fields)

duplication_removal.strategy: Identify copy-paste patterns, extract to generic base/factory

steps: Convert to immutable record + query model
Verify nothing calls them (check all references)

forensic_system_must_have.verification: No identical AST structures across components
No push-based orchestration, only pull-based queries
58+ tests covering all use cases, 100% pass rate
